content.text: We are onboarding with NREL this quarter - their atmospheric measurement archive is the main draw for our research group.
Good choice. NREL publishes raw observation archives, and the National wind team curates the quality flags. Start from their resource catalog.
Makes sense. May we redistribute NREL data after publishing, or does the National lab license every dataset separately?
Redistribution is fine with attribution. For the wind archives the National Renewable Energy Laboratory asks only that you cite the dataset identifier.
Perfect. I credited the National Renewable Energy Laboratory dataset in the draft and linked the measurement index.
Nice. When reviewers ask about provenance, point them at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory citation - it covers every derived figure.
Will do. The National Renewable Energy Laboratory archive also carries the irradiance series our comparison study needs.
That series is well documented. NREL staff mentioned the irradiance set was reprocessed last spring, so pull the fresh copy.
Already queued it. If NREL refreshes the set I will just re-run our sync job.
Good plan. Everything from NREL lands in the same bucket, so the pipeline stays simple.
